source_title: Luca Intersects 19 Metres of 6.3 g/t Gold Equivalent from the Creston Vein at Tahuehueto Mine
source_excerpt:
VANCOUVER, BC , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Luca Mining Corp. ("Luca" or the "Company") (TSXV: LUCA) (OTCQX: LUCMF ) (Frankfurt: Z68) is pleased to report new assay results from its ongoing 2026 exploration drill program at the Tahuehueto gold-silver mine in Durango, Mexico.
The latest results are highlighted by an intersection of 18.7 metres ("m") of 6.28 g/t gold equivalent (" AuEq "**) at the Creston Vein, which returned a wider and higher-grade mineralized interval than previously anticipated in the resource model. Located close to existing underground infrastructure, the intersection is within an area scheduled for mining during the first half of 2027 and has the potential to provide additional high-grade mill feed in the near term.
Additional high-grade results from the Catorce and Santiago veins continue to demonstrate the potential for near-mine resource expansion at Tahuehueto. At Catorce, an underexplored area interpreted to represent a southern extension of the Creston Vein system, drilling returned 13.7 m of 3.33 g/t AuEq and 3.6 m of 6.67 g/t AuEq . At Santiago, drilling intersected 11.6 m of 5.21 g/t AuEq as ongoing infill and step-out programs continue to define this growing mineralized system.

Exploration continues across multiple targets at Tahuehueto, with two contracted diamond drill rigs currently on site, an additional surface rig en route and Luca's underground Termite rig supporting near-term mineral definition. To date, the Company has completed 67 underground drillholes totalling 11,450 m and 38 surface drillholes totalling 7,236 m.
"These results continue to support our view that mineralization at Tahuehueto is continuous and that the broader system remains underexplored, with significant potential for further resource growth," stated Paul D. Gray, Vice President Exploration of Luca Mining. "The standout result of 18.7 metres at 6.28 g/t AuEq from the Creston Vein exceeded our previous interpretation of the zone in both width and grade. Importantly, this mineralization is located close to existing underground development, and we anticipate being able to bring this area into production in 2027, with the potential to improve mill head grades and mining efficiency given the width of the mineralized interval.
We are also encouraged by the continued high-grade results from Catorce and Santiago, which highlight the exploration potential across multiple vein systems at Tahuehueto. Looking ahead, our program will focus on continued definition drilling at Creston, Perdido, Catorce and Santiago, as well as testing the highly prospective gap between the Creston and Santiago vein systems. We believe these efforts can both support near-term mine planning and unlock additional resource growth across the property."
Drillholes DDH26-RCE-02 through DDG26-RCE-07 targeted mineralization previously identified within the Catorce Block, a known, but under-drilled Tahuehueto mineralized zone that is interpreted to be a southern extension of the Creston Vein System and has not seen any exploration efforts since 2008 (see Company News Release dated September 8, 2026).
Drillholes DDH26-SGO-10 through DDH26-SGO-12 targeted mineralization within the Santiago Vein through in-fill drilling bolstering 2025 drilling success in the zone (See Company News Releases dated September 8, 2025 and December 19, 2025).

As part of the Tahuehueto exploration program a Luca owned and operated Termite drill rig capable of drilling "BQ" sized drill core up to 100 m in length has been added to bolster near underground workings verification and mineral definition. Drill core from this drill rig are handled by the Tahuehueto exploration department and treated the same as exploration drill core (processing, logging and sampling) and is now being utilized to more accurately define the mineralized zones anticipated to be part of the near-term mine plan objectives. Drillholes TRT26-09 through TRT26-11 were drilled from Level 12 of the Tahuehueto mine and targeted the Perdido vein in areas that are scheduled to be mined during H1 2027. Drillholes TRT26-12 through TRT26-15 were drilled from Level 25 and targeted the Creston Vein in areas that are scheduled to be mined during H1 2027.
Of particular significance, drillhole TRT26-15 intersected a wider and higher-grade interval than previously anticipated within the Creston Vein, providing additional geological information that may support the inclusion of high-grade material in the Company's 2027 mine plan.

About 2026 Tahuehueto Exploration Program
The Tahuehueto property comprises a large epithermal gold-silver vein system with approximately 11 kilometres of known vein strike length and numerous mineralized structures. Mineralization remains open along strike and at depth across most modeled Mineral Resource areas. The current campaigns represent the first substantive exploration drilling conducted on the property in more than 12 years, and the first since the addition of key concessions to the land package (See Company News Release dated August 28, 2025).
Luca's 2026 exploration program builds on the success of the 2025 campaign. The program is designed to expand known mineral resources, adding near-term mineable material and defining the vertical and lateral extent of mineralization, as well as to identify additional thick, high-grade breccia zones known to occur within the epithermal vein system, and test multiple underexplored vein systems.
In addition to the four veins that currently support the mineral resource, at least 14 additional prospective veins have been documented within the concession area with potential to host epithermal Au-Ag (Â±Cu-Zn-Pb) mineralization. In several cases, these targets may represent extensions of the existing mineralized structures.
Overall, the Company has identified more than 11 km of prospective vein structures along strike, compared to approximately 4.5 km of mineralized veins incorporated into the current mineral resource model, highlighting significant exploration upside across the property.

Analytical Method and Quality Assurance/Quality Control Measures
All drill core splits reported in this news release were analyzed by Bureau Veritas of Durango, Mexico, utilizing the Multi-Acid digestion ICP-ES 35-element MA300 analytical package with FA-430 30-gram Fire Assay with AAS finish for gold on all samples. Au over-limits from FA-430 are re-analyzed by FA530 30-gram Fire Assay with Gravimetric finish. Ag over-limits from ICP MA300 analytical package are re-analyzed by FA530 30-gram Fire Assay with Gravimetric finish. Similarly, Cu, Pb and Zn over-limits from ICP MA300 analytical package are re-analyzed by ICP Multi-Acid digestion MA370 package. All core samples were split by core saw on-site at Luca's core processing facilities at the Tahuehueto Mine. Once split, half samples were placed back in the core boxes with the other half of split samples sealed in poly bags with one part of a three-part sample tag inserted within. Samples were collected by Bureau Veritas at the Tahuehueto Mine site and transported to Bureau Veritas' Durango Laboratory, where samples are prepared to a 250-gram pulp and analyzed for Gold by Fire assay with pulps shipped to Bureau Veritas's Analytical laboratory in Vancouver, B.C., for final ICP chemical analysis. A robust system of standards, 1/4 core duplicates and blanks were implemented in the 2024-2026 exploration drilling program and is monitored as chemical assay data become available.
